structures.name: Cingulate gyrus
objects: Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle anterior part).r
Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle posterior part).r
Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Posterior dorsal part).r

rows: Location
Medial surface of the hemisphere, arching just above the corpus callosum.
Function
Part of the limbic system: emotion, motivation, and attention.
hy: In subfalcine herniation the cingulate gyrus is pushed under the falx cerebri and can compress the anterior cerebral artery.

rows: Location
Uppermost of the three horizontal gyri of the frontal lobe, above the superior frontal sulcus. It continues onto the medial surface of the hemisphere.
Function
Planning of movement (its medial part holds the supplementary motor area) and higher mental functions such as working memory.
Location
Medial surface of the hemisphere around the upper end of the central sulcus, where the precentral and postcentral gyri continue over the upper margin.
Function
Motor and sensory cortex for the opposite leg and foot, and voluntary control of the bladder and bowel sphincters.
hy: It lies in anterior cerebral artery territory. A stroke of that artery causes weakness and loss of sensation in the opposite leg more than in the arm or face, and can cause urinary incontinence.

rows: Location
Medial surface of the parietal lobe, between the marginal part of the cingulate sulcus in front and the parieto-occipital sulcus behind.
Function
Association cortex concerned with visual and spatial processing, memory of events, and awareness of self.
Location
Wedge of the medial surface of the occipital lobe, between the parieto-occipital sulcus in front and the calcarine sulcus below.
Function
Its lower edge is the upper bank of the calcarine sulcus: primary visual cortex for the lower quarter of the opposite visual field.
hy: A lesion causes loss of the lower quarter of the opposite visual field in both eyes (inferior quadrantanopia).

rows: Location
Medial surface of the occipital lobe below the calcarine sulcus, continuing forward into the parahippocampal gyrus.
Function
Its upper edge is the lower bank of the calcarine sulcus: primary visual cortex for the upper quarter of the opposite visual field.
hy: A lesion causes loss of the upper quarter of the opposite visual field in both eyes (superior quadrantanopia).

rows: Location
Medial edge of the under surface of the temporal lobe, beside the midbrain. Its front end hooks back as the uncus, and the hippocampus lies just deep to it.
Function

Part of the limbic system. Through the entorhinal cortex at its front end it is the main route of information from the cortex into the hippocampus and back to the cortex, and so is needed to form new memories.
hy: In uncal herniation the uncus is pushed over the edge of the tentorium and presses on the oculomotor nerve, giving a fixed dilated pupil on that side, and on the cerebral peduncle, giving weakness of the opposite side of the body.

rows: Location
Most medial gyrus on the under surface of the frontal lobe, medial to the olfactory sulcus, in which the olfactory bulb and tract lie.
Function
Part of the prefrontal cortex on the orbital surface of the frontal lobe. Its particular function is not well defined.
Location
Thick band of white matter that arches over the lateral ventricles in the midline. From front to back: rostrum, genu, body, splenium.
Function
Connects matching areas of the two cerebral hemispheres.
Location
Deep groove on the medial surface of the occipital lobe, running forward from the occipital pole to meet the parieto-occipital sulcus.
Separates
Cuneus above from lingual gyrus below. The primary visual cortex lies in its two banks.
hy: The visual cortex here is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery. A stroke of that artery causes loss of the opposite half of the visual field in both eyes, often with sparing of central (macular) vision.

rows: Location
Medial surface of the hemisphere, running down and forward from the upper margin to meet the calcarine sulcus.
Separates
Parietal lobe (precuneus) in front from occipital lobe (cuneus) behind.

rows: Location
The back end of the cingulate sulcus, where it turns up to reach the upper margin of the hemisphere just behind the upper end of the central sulcus.
Separates
Paracentral lobule in front from precuneus behind.
